newsitem.title: NIGERIA: FORECAST-Nigeria bank chief sees 7.5 pct 97 growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Nigeria bank chief sees 7.5 pct 97 growth.

text.p: Nigeria's economy could grow by up to 7.5 percent next year, central bank governor Paul Ogwuma said in an interview published on Thursday.
Ogwuma told editors of the independent Thisday newspaper that Nigeria had achieved economic stability over the last year and would put in place reflationary policies next year.
"Having achieved economic stability, we expect the economy to grow in 1997," he said, adding "I would expect us to grow between five and 7.5 percent."
A recent central bank report said the nation's economy recorded some improvement in the first half of 1996.
Nigerian economists broadly agree with this view but say the modest improvement is yet to show in ordinary peoples' lives.
"A relationary policy aimed at creating jobs would be adopted," Ogwuma said, adding "This is expected to make the economy grow faster in 1997."
In 1995, Nigeria recorded a growth rate of only 2.2 percent, which economists consider is actually negative given the population's growth rate of 2.9 percent.
Ogwuma said a growth rate of about four percent was expected this year.

Military ruled Nigeria, which slumped into crisis in 1993 when the army annulled a presidential election to restore civil rule, has put in place liberal economic policies that have seen the exchange rate stabilise and inflation heading downwards.
But so far this has failed to attract foreign investment and the government has begun to aggresively campaign for investors.

It is also expected to embark on a major privatisation of key sectors of the economy including telecommunications, electricity generation and distribution as well the oil industry, the nation's economic backbone.
Thisday quoted other government officials as saying all terminally distressed banks would be liquidated next year to provide a clean slate for the privatisation programme.
